2011_029_110111regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of November 1, 2011, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Contents cover recognition items, the October 4 and October 18, 2011 minutes, the September 2011 Treasurer's Report and full check register, September year-to-date FY2012 budget reports, a Fall 2011/12 athletic equipment bid tabulation, and reports on iPad curriculum, MEAP/MME changes, the facilities study and the superintendent's goals. The central business item is the 2010-2011 audit presented by Teresa Pollock of Plante & Moran, which reports a General Fund balance of $19,756,837 at June 30, 2011.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, November 1, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW), Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognition**
- Heather Kelly, Troy High visual arts teacher, whose mixed-media "Wish Project" was displayed at Art Prize in Grand Rapids.
- Rebecca Brewer, AP biology teacher at Troy High, named a 2011 ING National Unsung Hero and awarded $27,000 for her "Mini-Med School: Simulating Surgeries" project for 11th and 12th grade students.
- Healthier U.S. School Challenge Bronze Award, granted March 30, 2011 to all twelve Troy elementary schools (Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles); each school received a banner, plaque and $500, and the district was invited to a White House reception on October 17, 2011. Presented with Sodexo's Gayle Moran and Sam Mozdzierz.
- Retirement of Robert Stromayer, Director of Niles Community Education, with the district since August 22, 1988, 23 years of service.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the October 4, 2011 meeting and October 18, 2011 workshop, the September 2011 Treasurer's Report, and a bid award for spring athletic supplies. The October 4 minutes record resolutions 11-091 through 11-097, all carried 6-0 with Mr. Hauff absent, including a network core bid to Netech for $105,388.50 and network area storage to CDWg for $636,000.00, both from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund.

**September YTD budget reports, fiscal 2012**
General Fund revenue of $127,175,517 approved with $18,672,228 actual and $108,503,289 uncollected (85.32 percent); expenditures of $128,282,487 approved with $17,038,843 actual, $86,938,615 encumbered and $24,305,029 available (18.95 percent). Excess revenue under expenditures of ($1,106,970); fund balance $18,803,870 at July 1, 2011 and $17,696,900 projected at June 30, 2012. Consolidated special revenue funds show ($86,702) and a balance moving from $1,937,173 to $1,850,471; debt service shows $960,385 and a balance from $518,484 to $1,478,869.

**2010-2011 audit (Plante & Moran)**
General Fund revenue $137,351,598 against expenditures $137,073,866, a net change in fund balance of $895,776, and an ending balance of $19,756,837. Instructional spending was 67 percent of expenditures at Troy versus an Oakland County average of 59 percent (county data from 2009-2010). Fund balance as a percentage of expenditures is charted at 14.41 percent for 2011 against a 2010 state average excluding Detroit Public Schools of 10.44 percent.

**Other items**
Personnel: a probationary 2011-2012 contract for Melissa Marsack, .5 FTE Great Start Readiness Preschool teacher at Hill Elementary. Curriculum reports on iPad integration (1000 laptops and 660 iPads in the technology replacement) and on higher MEAP and MME cut scores requiring roughly 65 percent correct answers instead of 39 percent. The 18-member Facilities Study Team, co-chaired by Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim, will present a recommendation on February 7, 2012. Bid 9720 for Fall 2011/12 athletic equipment is tabulated across ten bidders with no award recommendation printed.
2011_029_110111regmtg.verbose:
**Identification.** Troy School District Board of Education packet for the Regular Meeting of November 1, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; masthead address 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. The agenda runs recognition, consent agenda, personnel, curriculum reports on iPad lesson plans and MEAP/MME changes, the 2010-2011 audit, and reports on the facilities study and superintendent’s goals.

**Recognition.** Heather Kelly, Troy High visual arts teacher, had her mixed-media "Wish Project" chosen for Art Prize in Grand Rapids. Rebecca Brewer, Advanced Placement biology teacher at Troy High School, was named the nation’s most innovative educator in the 2011 ING National Unsung Heroes Awards Program and given a check for $27,000 for "Mini-Med School: Simulating Surgeries," moving 11th and 12th grade biology students to mock surgical procedures. The Food Service Department received the Healthier U.S. School Challenge Bronze Award, granted March 30, 2011 for all twelve elementary schools — Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass and Wattles — with Troy and Birmingham Public Schools the only two Michigan districts qualifying every elementary school, both partnered with Sodexo; presenters were Gayle Moran and Sam Mozdzierz of Sodexo, and each school received a banner, plaque and $500 plus an invitation to a White House reception on October 17, 2011. Administrator recognition went to Robert Stromayer, Director of Niles Community Education, serving since August 22, 1988, 23 years.

**October 4, 2011 minutes.** President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present, Mr. Hauff absent, Superintendent Fowler, administrators including Machesky, Mull and Rajter, and approximately 55 audience members. More than 350 students were honored by the College Board. Resolution 11-091 recognized the 2011-2012 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, signed the fourth day of October, 2011, semifinalist status being the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT. Elizabeth Brooks of the Michigan Association for Gifted Children presented the Nicholas Green Distinguished Student Award, a $500 U.S. savings bond, to Brittany Ngia of Boulan Park Middle School. Resolution 11-092 approved the consent agenda; 11-093 approved probationary contracts for Elizabeth Crawford, Noah Elkins and Lauren Gardner; 11-094 seated the Sex Education Advisory Board co-chaired by Larry Hahn and Nicole Jenkins; 11-095 awarded the network core bid to Netech for $105,388.50 and 11-096 awarded network area storage to CDWg for $636,000.00, both as 2004 Capital Projects Fund expenditures. Mr. Rajter reported the $470 permanent reduction in the foundation allowance per student and the one-time $100 per pupil adjustment conditioned on adopting four of five Best Practices, including charging employees at least 10% of health care premiums, and noted 27 education bills sent to the House and 23 to the Senate. Resolution 11-097 moved the board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(h) at 9:05 p.m., reconvening at 9:10 p.m.; every vote was 6 ayes, 0 nays, Hauff absent, and the meeting adjourned at 9:31 p.m. The October 18, 2011 workshop opened at 6:00 p.m. with Ms. Pollack and Ms. Edwards of Plante & Moran present, covering facility planning, the audit, foundations of special education (IDEA, Michigan Administrative Rules for Special Education, the Oakland County ISD Plan), all-day kindergarten and administrator evaluation, adjourning at 9:55 p.m. Minutes were submitted by Secretary Paula Fleming.

**September 2011 Treasurer’s Report.** Submitted by Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. Check register printed by Pentamation Enterprises, report ACCTPA21, on 10/05/2011, selecting cash accounts A1001 through A1005 and check dates 09/01/2011 through 09/30/2011, accounting period 4/12. **Notable checks and wires.** MESSA check 296073, October 2011 premium $978,109.66 plus COBRA $1,866.70, total $979,976.36; Oakland County Treasurer check 295688, General Fund tax debit $275,042.58 against a $16,706.11 credit for $258,336.47, the same check carrying debt-fund totals of $46,406.92, $16,237.39 and $4,438.80; Houghton Mifflin check 295894, $139,981.76; Sungard Public Sector check 295808, $106,893.01; Inacomp Technical Services check 295896, $52,290.00; Judson Center check 295763 for ESY tuition, $41,190.00; Netech Corp check 295686, $40,962.90; R K A Petroleum check 295944 fuel, $39,738.44; Plante & Moran check 295690 audit services, $30,000.00; Cleveland Corporate check 296106, $26,816.24; Lear Corporation check 295905, $26,013.65; Zip Mail Services check 296138 postage escrow, $20,000.00; Safe Ed LLC check 295953 security, $19,541.00; Direct Energy gas for Troy High $19,025.71 and Athens $15,438.73; SchoolDude.com check 295955, $18,437.25. Wires include MPSERS payments of $710,146.39 and $762,392.38, payroll taxes of $760,398.08 and $803,143.03, and VRIP payments of $85,437.60 on two dates.

**2010-2011 audit, Teresa Pollock of Plante & Moran, year ended June 30, 2011.** General Fund revenue $137,351,598 and expenditures $137,073,866, excess $277,732, transfers in $721,905 and out ($103,861), net change $895,776, fund balance $18,861,061 to $19,756,837. Special revenue funds $5,361,781 revenue, $4,904,690 expenditures, excess $457,091, transfers out ($618,044), net change ($160,953), balance $2,039,030 to $1,878,077. Capital project funds revenue $20,783, expenditures $3,711,105, net change ($3,690,322), balance $8,229,662 to $4,539,340. Debt service revenue $18,122,030, expenditures $18,669,233, net change ($547,203), balance $780,922 to $233,719. General Fund revenue budget versus actual: total $137,530,238 versus $137,351,598; local $43,333,461 versus $43,169,049; state $72,966,234 versus $73,988,119; federal $13,007,711 versus $11,947,217; other $8,222,832 versus $8,247,213. Expenditures: total $138,128,536 versus $137,073,866; instruction $92,866,638 versus $91,468,454; support and other $44,026,943 versus $44,330,747; community $1,234,955 versus $1,274,665. Instructional expenditures were 67% at Troy against an Oakland County average of 59%, county data from 2009-2010. The historical fund balance chart labels $40,688,281 (footnoted to a $9 million land sale), $31,043,131 (a retirement rate increase of 14% with no revenue increase and a $5.5 million ERI), $20,594,715 (a $4.9 million ERI), $19,756,837, $18,861,061, $8,156,942, plus $35,294,218, $28,896,195, $30,027,579 and $29,807,152. Fund balance as a percentage of expenditures is charted at 31.40%, 22.89%, 21.71%, 22.25%, 21.83%, 14.09%, 13.70%, 14.41%, and a 2010 state average excluding DPS of 10.44%, against the MSBO Recommended Operating FB band and an 8% Borrowing Danger Zone. Item 8.B asks the board to accept and approve the audited 2011 financial statements.

**Personnel and curriculum.** Item 6.A recommends a probationary 2011-2012 contract for Melissa Marsack, .5 FTE Great Start Readiness Preschool Teacher at Hill Elementary School; B.S. in Elementary Education, Oakland University, December 2005; Michigan Provisional Certificate March 2006; kindergarten teacher at Prevail Academy, Mount Clemens, September 2007 to June 2011; resident of Clinton Township. Ron Keolian, Coordinator of Instructional Technology, and Merri Lynn Colligan, Director of Technology, reported on the iPad Integration Committee: technology replacement of 1000 laptops and 660 iPads plus virtualization to the Troy Cloud, iOS 5, covered cases and carts with Care Kits and a Projector; ten pilot teachers were named, with next steps including special education piloting in MICI and RR at Bemis and autism work at Morse and Hamilton. Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, reported that the State Board of Education adopted more rigorous MEAP and MME cut scores in September, so students need roughly 65 percent of answers correct to pass instead of the previous 39 percent benchmark, with Smarter Balance computer adaptive assessments of the Common Core first administered in 2015 and full implementation in 2014-2015; consortium requirements cite the Federal Register, Vol. 75, No. 68, April 9, 2010, pp. 18171-85.

**Facilities study, superintendent’s goals and Bid 9720.** The Facilities Study Team of 18 community members — Rahmat Awan, Greg Bryen, David Cole, Scott Courtney, Adeyinka Dawodu, Jamie Douglas, Waqar Hashim, Laurie Huber, Dale Jerome, Lynda Keough, Bernard Lourin, John Mayernik, Denise Murray, Heather Plastow, Kim Rosseter, Nehal Shah, Pete va der Harst and Pete Ziegenfelder — is co-chaired by Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim, held planning meetings October 28-29, met November 2 on enrollment and district financial status, and will present a recommendation at the February 7, 2012 board meeting. Dr. Fowler gave the first of four updates on 2011-2012 superintendent goals, the next due January 17, 2012, covering visibility (PTO/PTA presentations begun October 10 and complete by January 20, 2012; staff presentations begun October 19 and complete by January 19, 2012), the facilities study, a data processing cost analysis phased September 2011 through June 2012, career and college readiness, the LAC-O Best Practices Conference of January 27, 2012, and communications via TS-TV and a new district website in February 2012. Bid 9720 for Fall 2011/12 athletic equipment tabulates ten bidders — Cannon Sports Inc., Aluminum Athletic Equipment, Flaghouse Inc., Dimmer Warren Enterprises, Pyramid School Products, M-F Athletics, ForSports, Sport Supply Group, S & S Worldwide and Riddell/All American — for Athens, Troy High and Boulan Park Middle School programs, with no award recommendation or low-bid designation printed.
